name: Udaipur
tagline: Rajasthan's city of lakes and palaces
summary: Udaipur's white palaces rise from the shores of Lake Pichola, with an island palace floating in the middle. The old city is a tangle of havelis, temples and rooftop restaurants, and the hill forts of Kumbhalgarh are a day's trip away.
seasonNote: October to March is ideal; the lakes are fullest just after the monsoon. Summer is hot; the monsoon (July to September) is green and quiet.
arrival: Udaipur airport is 30 minutes from the old city, with flights from Delhi and Mumbai. Trains run from Jaipur and Delhi.
gettingAround: Walk the old city lanes; rickshaws and taxis for further sights.
cashTip: UPI and cards are common; carry cash for boats and small shops.
foodTip: Rajasthani thalis with dal baati churma, gatte ki sabzi and laal maas, best eaten on a lakeside rooftop at sunset.
buyTip: Miniature paintings, silver jewellery, block-printed textiles and leather from the old-city lanes.
baseArea: The old city near Lal Ghat and Gangaur Ghat, or Hanuman Ghat across the lake

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
items.summary: A 15th-century hill fort whose walls run for 36 km, among the longest in the world.
items.expect: About 2.5 hours each way; combine with the Ranakpur Jain temple.
items.tip: Leave early and see Ranakpur's marble temple on the way.
